item.title: Why can people with low bad cholesterol still have heart attacks?
item.description: A study has uncovered a concerning relationship between lipoproteins, particularly triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a), and the risk of developing coronary artery disease. Analyzing nearly 3,000 blood proteins, it revealed key differences in protein patterns compared to LDL cholesterol. The results underscore the importance of inflammation and vascular changes in coronary artery disease progression, indicating the necessity for additional research to better understand these proteins' influence on cardiovascular health.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Christie’s Auction Withdrawal: Christie’s pulled Kahlo painting; 1953 return complicates export claims
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, a rare Frida Kahlo painting was pulled from a New York auction at Christie’s. The auction house raised concerns over the artwork's ownership provenance, especially its ties to Kahlo's iconic Casa Azul. Mexican officials are now on the hunt for necessary documentation to verify its legal status, with Christie’s optimistic about reintroducing the piece after thorough investigations.

item.title: Bristol's 600-year-old Ashton Court Mansion could finally be restored after councillors backed a 125-year lease to a community trust, but the group has raised only £125,000 toward its early funding target
item.description: Ashton Court Mansion, a historic building in Bristol, has been neglected and is in poor condition. The Bristol City Council has approved a 125-year lease for the Ashton Court Mansion Trust. The trust aims to restore the mansion and enhance community access, with a financial target of £480,000. They have raised £125,000 through a community share offer, showcasing public interest in the project.

item.title: Prosecution Withdrawal: Powys Council drops case; renovation approval remains unconfirmed
item.description: A group of four friends took on a challenging planning dispute with Powys County Council after acquiring Llanerchydol Hall. Their efforts, including an investment of £700,000, led to the withdrawal of the council's case just before trial. This historic mansion, built in 1776, boasts rich heritage, and the owners' goal is to create a sustainable business by welcoming guests into completed rooms. However, the comprehensive restoration remains an ongoing project.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: America’s rarest fish is bouncing back: Biologists diving into Nevada’s Devils Hole counted 137 pupfish this fall, nearly double the 69 found a year earlier in the only place the species lives in the wild
item.description: Devils Hole pupfish, a rare species, has seen population numbers increase significantly after a near extinction event. Recent surveys indicated 137 individual fish, more than doubling from previous counts. Conservation efforts, including releasing captive-raised fish, have contributed to the recovery of their population. Despite positive signs, challenges such as environmental disturbances and habitat vulnerability remain a concern for their future.

item.title: Trump's $48.3b Iran war bill excludes damaged US bases; Democrats press for tally
item.description: The financial cost of the US war against Iran has reached an estimated $48.3 billion. Lawmakers are urging the Pentagon to provide assessments of damages to military bases. Democratic senator Richard Blumenthal pressed for damage estimates during a Senate Armed Services Committee meeting. According to reports, Iranian attacks have resulted in billions of dollars in losses, including damage to key facilities.

item.title: French woman’s €20 flea market find fetches €251,000
item.description: A woman from France stumbled upon a remarkable black ceramic lamp at a local brocante for only €20. Months later, her daughter discovered an inscription revealing the lamp was crafted by Georges Jouve. They reached out to a Paris auction house, which confirmed its authenticity. This led to a stunning auction result of €251,000, setting a record for a Jouve lamp.

item.title: A nuclear blast might be humanity’s best shot at nudging a killer asteroid off course
item.description: In an intriguing twist of space science, researchers are exploring nuclear explosions as a potential solution to divert asteroids threatening Earth. Their latest simulations reveal that the angle of X-ray emissions plays a crucial role in determining how effective these deflections may be. With diverse asteroid shapes adding complexity to the challenge, the developing model aims to offer improved predictions of how asteroids will respond to such drastic measures.

item.title: Isolated tribe Awá emereges from Brazilian Amazon forest amid alarming threats by illegal invaders
item.description: Recently, the elusive Awá tribe, famed for their isolation, reached out to a neighboring settlement in the Arariboia Indigenous territory. In search of food and assistance, their visit exposed the severe impacts of illegal land encroachments. Local villagers documented the meeting, bringing attention to the perils that Indigenous people face. Advocacy groups are demanding stronger safeguards and acknowledgment of the rights of uncontacted tribes to preserve their way of life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US prosecutor declines charges against white cop who killed Black man
item.description: A police officer in Wisconsin will not be charged for fatally shooting a Black man in July. Prosecutor Ismael Ozanne concluded that the officer acted reasonably in the situation involving Corey Ruiz. Ruiz allegedly resisted arrest, brandished a knife, and was unaffected by Tasers before he was shot. Family members of Ruiz criticized the decision and claimed excessive force was used in the incident.
